name: 14097-longprompt-7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
architecture: dense decoder (Starcoder2ForCausalLM), 32 layers, 36 query heads, 4 KV heads, head_dim 128, bf16; 7.17B params, ~14.3 GB of weights, and it downloads.
load_profile: poisson, rate=8 req/s, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%. The rate is above capacity on purpose, so the measurement is completion throughput under sustained overload.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`, single turn, no shared prefix: 8192 prompt tokens and 250 output tokens, both fixed with min=max, 500 requests bounded. `request_format: plain`, because this checkpoint is a base code model with no chat template in tokenizer_config.json. Expect the engine's reported prompt_token_ids to sit within a token or two of 8192 rather than exactly on it: the synthetic prompt is built by encoding and decoding, and the engine re-tokenizes the resulting string.
purpose: A code completion service for whole-file prompts, handling eight long requests per second on one GPU.
launch:
# Launch config for 14097-longprompt-7b-1gpu. Every argument below is valid for the engine at
# `commit_id`; a key from a later vLLM is a TypeError at engine construction.

model: bigcode/starcoder2-7b
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 16384

# PINNED AND LOAD-BEARING. `vllm serve` picks 8192 on an H100 at this commit, but an engine built
# in-process reports a usage context absent from that table and falls through to the scheduler
# default of 2048, quartering the per-step token budget. 8192 is what "unpinned" meant here.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

max-num-seqs: 1024
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
block-size: 16
num-gpu-blocks-override: 4096
enable-prefix-caching: true
